findings.text: count_live_names_without_source re-implements the population enumeration owned by imas_codex/standard_names/source_invariant.py:141 find_sourceless_live_names and imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_supersession.py:3045 classify_sourceless_standard_names, sharing only the predicate builders, so the package now has a third reader of the same population and its liveness rule can drift from the other two; it duplicates rather than extends either owner.

The headline prints report['count'] (9, with the exempt derived parent subtracted) beside live_names 3,266 and live_with_producer 3,256, whose difference is live_without_producer 10, so the command reports a self-contradictory count; the committed docs/evidence/fragments/sn-catalog-consistency/scc-live-names-without-a-source.json carries count 9 beside live_without_producer 10 and tests/standard_names/test_source_reads.py:226 compares only key sets, so this survives the guard.

source_paths_projection returns every producer including stale ones while imas_codex/standard_names/source_invariant.py:40 producerless_cypher treats a stale producer as none, so the planted name reads_stale_source at tests/standard_names/test_source_reads.py:108 answers a source from search and read_source_paths yet is listed by the count as having none, and the one-rule claim is untested for that shape.

The live_children expression restates the child name_stage and status lists owned by imas_codex/standard_names/source_invariant.py:11 _live_child_cypher, because it needs a count rather than EXISTS, so the derived-parent exemption that decides whether a name is counted can drift from the export gate's.

The page states find_sourceless_live_names returned the identical 9 ids over all 3,266 live ids, but no EXIT-bearing log in /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261114T211624671239-scc-sources-read-from-one-place records that call: measure-live-population.py prints only the command's own output and the copy-versus-edge divergence, so the done_when's same-job direct read rests on prose.
